articleTitle: Synchronization algorithm of quantum key distribution system with protection from unauthorized access
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The two pass auto compensation quantum key distribution system (QKDS) with phase-encoded states of photons in synchronization mode are studied. The algorithm of synchronization QKDS, presupposing the division of the repetition period of the optical pulses on the time windows and the detection of the signal window are offered. The peculiarity of the algorithm is that it is implemented in the single-photon mode, increasing the security of synchronization mode. The second feature of the algorithm is that when equal numbers of accumulated pulses in two adjacent time windows, a decision for admission photon pulse in any of the windows, if the number of accumulated pulses in it exceeds the number of detected pulses in the other windows. In a certain algorithm in this case, both windows were “noises” that was the reason for missing the signal window. Modeling algorithm found that when the number of time windows from 2 to 1024, the difference of the limiting values of the probability does not exceed 3.34%. The requirements with respect to the duration of the time window and the photon momentum are formulated. It is shown that increasing the number of time windows from 2 to 1024 implies reducing the probability of less than 2% while maintaining the time of uncertainty in relation of emergence the photon pulse 512 times. An analytical expression for the calculation of the probability of correct detection of the signal time window in the proposed synchronization algorithm QKDS.

articleTitle: Identification of cost and energy efficient multiplexing techniques for LR-PON for different network scenario
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: With the increasing bandwidth demand, passive optical network is considered as the most suitable and promising candidate to support the future access networks. In this paper, we analyze and identify the most appropriate remote node combination for different network scenarios for different fiber reach and subscribers. We cascade the power splitter and arrayed waveguide grating (AWG) at remote to give hybrid TDM-WDM PON. Hybrid multiplexing provides efficient use of optical line terminal (OLT) resources and reduces the required wavelengths and transceivers. Reduction in wavelength and transceivers results in designing energy and cost effective access network. This study will help the network operators to choose the most appropriate remote node architecture to give economic and environmental friendly services for different network scenario.

articleTitle: LSPR based fiber optic sensor for detection of E. coli using bacteriophage T4
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The aim of this study is to develop a localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) based scheme for pathogen detection using bacteriophages as recognition elements. The detection was performed using a portable optical set up consisting of white light source, gold nanoparticles (AuNP) coated U bent fiber optic probe and a spectrometer. In this scheme, bacteria were immobilized non-specifically on gold coated fiber probes and the phages were allowed to interact with the bound bacteria on the probe. Since phages react with specific bacterial strains, the proposed scheme can be employed in specific bacteria detection.

articleTitle: Detection of on-off keying over weak atmospheric turbulence channels in free-space optics
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of detection of on-off keying signals in free-space optical communication links over weak atmospheric turbulence conditions, which causes variations in the intensity and phase of the received light signal. Fading in signal due to the weak atmospheric turbulence can be modeled by a lognormal distribution, to a sufficient degree of accuracy. Assuming only the knowledge of statistics of fading, we derive the near-optimal, blind detection rule exploiting the fact that the parameter of the lognormal distribution is small in practice. We also obtain the expression for the corresponding detection threshold in closed-form. This simple technique offers benefits over other existing detection strategies, as it has a low computational complexity. Through Monte Carlo simulations, we validate the accuracy of our expressions, and show that the performances of the optimal detector and the derived detector are nearly equal for low parameter values.

articleTitle: Designing a refractive index based biosensor using a photonic quasi-crystal fiber
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We design a ten-fold photonic quasi-crystal fiber using finite element method. Further, we explore various optical characteristics and exploit them for realizing a biosensor. We achieve a maximum refractive index sensitivity of 29000 nm/RIU and a resolution of 3.4 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> RIU a sensing range of 1.47-1.48.

articleTitle: Differentiator based frequency detector for 100-Gb/s analog domain DP-QPSK coherent optical receivers
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: One of the significant issues in coherent optical communication systems is the frequency offset between the carrier laser and the local oscillator (LO) laser. For the synchronization of the phase and frequency between the two lasers a carrier phase recovery and compensation (CPRC) circuit is required. A CPRC circuit that has a phase detector alone may fail to recover the carrier signal if the frequency offset is too large. A frequency detector is needed along with the phase detector in the CPRC circuit for achieving frequency acquisition. We propose a differentiator based FD for correcting the frequency offset. The proposed FD has been designed and simulated using 130 nm BiCMOS technology. A decision-assisted Costas loop based CPRC circuit that has the proposed FD is capable of compensating a frequency offset from -100 MHz to 100 MHz. The circuit is shown to achieve frequency acquisition in a 100-Gb/s dual polarization-quadrature phase shift keying (DP-QPSK) receiver when the laser line width was 200 kHz and the transmission was done over 80 km-long single mode fiber.

articleTitle: Modeling and simulation of opto-fluidic based Mach-Zehnder interferometer for biosensing application
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this paper, the integrated optical Mach-Zehnder Interferometer (IO-MZI) is designed for Biosensing application. A sensor arm with optical sensor with a liquid core waveguide in one of the optical path is considered for a Mach-Zehnder Interferometer. In this work an Integrated optical Mach-Zehnder Interferometeric biosensor is proposed for Rapid diagnostic test (RDT). The design of IO-MZI is done using COMSOL software.

articleTitle: Limited feedback of principal modes for high speed multimode fiber links
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Multimode fibers are widely used for short and medium haul links. However, the data rates through multimode fibers (MMFs) is limited due to modal dispersion. Recently, it has been shown that signaling in the set of “principal modes” (PMs) of the MMF can reduce dispersion significantly. However, accurate knowledge of the PMs is required at the transmitter to utilize them effectively. In this paper, we propose the use of Grassmannian line packing as a quantization scheme for communicating the PMs to the transmitter, and describe various codebook designs for few-mode and large-core MMFs. Simulations reveal that the channel frequency response can be improved by 5 dB for few-mode fibers and 2 dB for large-core MMFs using quantized PMs.

articleTitle: Temperature insensitive waveguide grating based SOI MOEMS accelerometer
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A simulation model of temperature insensitive waveguide grating based SOI MOEMS accelerometer is presented. The sensor consists of two waveguide gratings are placed on the beams suspending silicon micromachined proof mass. The gratings are placed on the beams suspending the micromachined silicon proof mass such that they have different linear chirp coefficient depending on their position on the beam. For small range of acceleration and temperature variations, the cross-sensitivity terms are ignored and by measuring the shift in Bragg wavelength of both gratings the external acceleration can be accurately measured. The resolution for the sensor is 0.001g with range of measurement of 1g.

articleTitle: Studies on the stability of regenerated fiber Bragg gratings at 1100 °C
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This paper presents studies on the long term thermal stability of regenerated fiber Bragg gratings (FBGs) at 1100 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C. The seed type-I FBGs of almost similar reflectivity (∼ 35 dB) were inscribed in hydrogen loaded fused silica fibers using high repetition rate (5.5 kHz) 255 nm UV radiation. These FBGs were subjected to multi-step annealing process upto 1100 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C spanning over 60 hours for regeneration and stabilisation of regenerated grating. The residual reflectivity of 40% and 10% was obtained for Ge doping of 3 mol% and 18 mol% respectively, which was stable even after ∼10 hours annealing at 1100 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C.

articleTitle: Aberration correction for transport of intensity phase imaging
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Transport of intensity phase imaging suffers from phase aberration due to presence of noise in experimental data and aberration induced by optical system. This induced low frequency aberration corrupts the original phase and makes it difficult to use for any further quantitative processing. In this paper an aberration correction scheme is proposed. A polynomial model is used to represent the low frequency induced aberrations, and further subtracted from the corrupted phase for correcting the phase profile. The proposed scheme is implemented on experimental data obtained from a static microstructure phase object, of 100 nanometer height. The results obtained from the proposed scheme shows a good agreement with the actual known values.

articleTitle: Ultra low-cost optical biosensor based on guided mode resonance grating filter
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Design and development of ultra low-cost, disposable devices for point-of-care diagnostics is the focus of scientific community in these days. In this work we propose a simple fabrication strategy, using non-conventional, low-cost, polycarbonate based micro-structured device which is supposed to be a low-cost, but highly sensitive sensing device for disposable bio-applications. The initial studies focused on the possibility of finding the concentration of sugar, the analyte, in honey being the sample using guided mode resonance grating filter (GMRGF) based biosensor, for both homogeneous as well as surface sensing. The sensitivity of 142nm/RIU and 23nm/RIU has been observed for homogeneous and surface sensing respectively.

articleTitle: Effect of intensity noise on stimulated Raman scattering in high power fiber lasers and amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Stimulated Raman Scattering is one of the primary nonlinearities limiting power scaling of high power fiber lasers and amplifiers. Conversion of signal light into the Raman generated Stokes component can result in several undesirable consequences such as temporal instabilities, spurious pulsing, beam quality degradation, focusing errors etc. most of which are catastrophic for the laser system. In this work, we investigate a novel and important aspect of Raman scattering in fiber lasers and amplifiers. Owing to intrinsic intensity noise at high powers, we demonstrate that the actual Raman gain can be substantially higher than the expected values calculated from mean powers. Using a physical model for intensity noise, we demonstrate very interesting connections between the laser bandwidth, dispersion in fiber and the actual Raman gain. This work enables further power scaling by providing design methodologies to control Raman scattering in fiber lasers and amplifiers.

articleTitle: Gain equilization of six mode groups using trench-assisted annular core EDFA
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Space division multiplexing (SDM) demands the development of the Few-mode erbium doped fiber amplifier (FM-EDFA). In this article, we propose a trench-assisted annular core EDFA using extra annulus doping for the gain equalization of six signal mode groups LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub>, LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>, LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub>, LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">31</sub>, LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">41</sub> and LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">51</sub>. The simulations confirm that the trenches help in reducing the differential modal gain (DMG). Thus, the proposed configuration would be useful for SDM based optical communication system.

articleTitle: DC electric field measurement using FBG sensor
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The paper presents theoretical analysis and experimental verification of a fiber Bragggrating based sensor for measurement of DC electric fields using a PZT sensor. This improves the physical understanding of field distribution in air medium around high voltage apparatus.

articleTitle: Imaging artificially induced dental caries using optical coherence tomography near 800 and 1300 nm region
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The Optical coherence tomography (OCT) based technique is proposed and demonstrated for determining the progress of dental caries. A conventional OCT system was setup in-house and was used to image natural caries, artificial caries and secondary caries with a resolution of 6.26 pm and 12.30 pm corresponding to 840 nm and 1310 nm, respectively. Dental caries were simulated artificially by mimicking the acidity of the oral cavity and imaged at different time intervals for upto 60 hours of demineralisation. The caries progression was estimated from the OCT images by measuring the thickness of the scattering and was found to be 45 to 50 micrometer deep in the 840 nm imaging and 40 to 48 micrometer deep for 1310 nm imaging for 60 hours of demineralisation. The same study was performed in an accelerated demineralisation environment in order to study the progression of caries and was found to be 200 to 210 micrometer deep for 68 hours of demineralisation.

articleTitle: Reversible ripple carry adder using the electro-optic effect of lithium-niobate based Mach-Zehnder interferometer
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In the present scenario, reversible logic design is receiving great attention due to its abilities in reducing the power dissipation, increasing the processing speed and accommodating higher densities in integrated circuits. There is a one-to-one mapping between inputs and outputs, due to which there is no loss of information. Many researchers have shown their interest in implementing reversible logic gates in optical domain using semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA). But, SOA has a major limitation of gain saturation, which they have not taken into account. In this paper, an n-bit reversible ripple carry adder using the electro-optic effect of lithium niobate based Mach-Zehnder Interferometer structure is proposed, which overcome the above mentioned limitation.

articleTitle: Modes of a planar optical waveguide truncated with perfectly matched layer: Collocation method
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A collocation scheme is presented to find the modes of a planar optical waveguide truncated with perfectly matched layer (PML). The method generates the eigenvalues for different modes namely guided, leaky modes and PML modes. Here, waveguide modes are studied without PML and with PML.

articleTitle: Femtosecond nonlinear optical properties of as grown and annealed Phthalocyanines thin films
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The nonlinear optical (NLO) properties of Tetra-tert-butyl-phthalocyanine (H2PC), Copper (II) Tetra-tert-butyl-phthalocyanine (CuPc) and Zinc (II) Tetra-tert-butyl-Phthalocyanine (ZnPC) thin films have been measured by using a single beam Z-scan technique with 250 fs laser pulse of 1064 nm central wavelength at a repetition rate of 664 KHz. The choice of Phthalocyanines (Pc) amongst other organic thin films for NLO properties is essentially motivated by architectural flexibility, high thermal stability and the ease of tailoring their physical and chemical properties. The observed nonlinear absorption (NLA) in Pc thin films at 1064 nm may be explained by using a model that includes Q band transition. The results showed that NLA increases on annealing the as prepared Pc films. This could be because of aggregation of Pc molecules on annealing. We found that nonlinear refractive index is affected by the nature of the central metal atom. Nonlinear refractive index values for CuPc are negative as compared to positive values for ZnPc and H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Pc. We also observed nonlinear optical switching and the presence of large fifth order nonlinearity in as prepared H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Pc films which could be attributed to two photon absorption (TPA) generated excited state refraction (ESR).

articleTitle: Fractal tree plasmonic nanoantenna array for multispectral surface-enhanced spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Plasmonic nanoantenna are pushing the sensitivity and detection limits of chemical and biochemical assay technologies. The challenge is to precisely tailor the spectral lineshapes and operational bandwidth and to engineer the localized electromagnetic field enhancements (“hot spots”) optimally for a particular spectroscopic task. Here we present a numerical study of the optical behavior of ternary tree fractal plasmonic gold nanoantenna. Spectral features spanning the visible to mid IR range are seen with the observation of characteristic self-similar features as the fractal order increases. The geometrical regularity of the ternary tree is perturbed and its influence on the optical properties is studied. The nanoantenna is seen to exhibit reduced polarization sensitivity even in highly assymetric structures. The intriguing optical properties of ternary tree fractal nanoantenna are particularly promising for the optimal design of substrates for performing multispectral surface-enhanced spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Four bit priority encoder using lithium niobate based Mach-Zehnder interferometers
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The efficient application of electro-optic effect in Lithium Niobate based Mach-Zehnder Interferometer to construct a four bit priority encoder has been demonstrated. Priority encoder has an advantage over a traditional encoder that it can identify the priority of the request signals appearing at the same time. The study has been carried out by simulating the proposed device using mathematical description and Beam propagation method.

articleTitle: Overhead projector transparency sheets as inexpensive wave plates: A Mueller matrix analysis
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We experimentally investigate anisotropy properties of commercial overhead projector transparency sheets using the Stokes-Mueller formalism and characterize the sheets in terms of coefficients of linear, diagonal and circular anisotropy, phase retardation, optic axis orientation, diattenuation and polarizance. We conclude by demonstrating that they can be used as inexpensive half and quarter wave plates.

articleTitle: Comparison of SERS activity of sputtered, electroless-plated and nanoparticle-coated plastic fiber optic probes
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Surface Enhanced Raman Scattering (SERS) spectroscopy is a promising tool for trace molecule analysis. Substrate development plays a crucial role in determining the SERS signal enhancement and the analyte detection limits. In this study, Plastic fiber optic (POF, 0.75 mm fiber diameter) U-bent probes coated with plasmonic gold obtained by three different approaches, namely sputtering, electroless-plating and Au nanoflower (AuNF) chemisorption are compared for their SERS activity using thiophenol as a model Raman analyte. The minimally sputtered probes produced detectable analyte peaks at low power but with lower enhancement. Substrates with increased sputter deposition times provided better enhancement. However, the AuNF-coated probes gave maximum SERS enhancement even at low power.

articleTitle: Demonstrating a nano viscometer using femtosecond laser induced photo-thermal effect
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We present a new method to utilize photo-thermal effect at nano-volume dimension, to measure viscosity, which could be useful to eventually correlate to in-vivo conditions. We present our measurements using high repetition rate low average power femtosecond laser induced conditions under which the photo-thermal effect is highly influence by the convective mode of heat transfer. This is especially important in absorbing liquids. This is unlike the typical photo-thermal conditions not involving such ultrashort pulses. Typical thermal processes involve only conductive mode of heat transfer and are phenomenological in nature. Inclusion of convective mode results in some additional molecular characteristics to the thermal process. We measure the traditional thermal lens studies with femtosecond pulse train through geometric beam divergence of a collimated laser beam co-propagating with the focused heating laser beam. The refractive index gradient in the sample due to the focused heating laser creates a thermal lens, which is measured. On the other hand, the same heat gradient from the focusing heating laser beam generates a change in local viscosity in the medium, which changes the trapped stiffness of an optically trapped microsphere in its vicinity. We use co-propagating femtosecond train of laser pulses of wavelength 1560 nm and 780 nm for these experiments. From the bulk thermal studies, we show that use of water as sample provides us the advantage to use conductive mode of heat transfer even with femtosecond pulse train excitation.

articleTitle: Optical surface states at the interface between a metal and dielectric nanophotonic structure
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We have studied theoretically the formation of novel optical Tamm states at the interface between a metal nano-layer and one-dimensional dielectric photonic crystal. We have used transfer matrix method to study the mode formation at the interface between the metal and dielectric nanophotonic structures. Unlike the conventional optical surface states, optical Tamm states can be excited at normal incidence of light. They can also be excited for TE polarized light. The tunability of optical Tamm states and the factors effecting their formation is studied in detail. Our results have applications in non-linear optics and in optical communication.

articleTitle: Subwavelength optical confinement and long propagation using grating based hybrid plasmonic waveguide with ultra-high nonlinearity
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A grating based hybrid plasmonic waveguide with subwavelength optical confinement and larger propagation length is proposed. The grating assisted low-loss guiding of hybrid plasmonic-photonic mode is achieved with high nonlinearity of 18.7 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>w<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. An acceptably low propagation loss of 4 dB/mm and hence a large propagation length of 1027-μm with modal area of 0.00017/μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> are reported.

articleTitle: 2×40 Gbps WDM-PON long haul system using FBG and Dicode
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this work, the effects of reshaped specta of different schemes such as NRZ (Non return to zero), Dicode-NRZ and Duobinary on Wavelength division multiplexing have been analysed for two wavelength 1550 & 1551 nm with the system capacity of 80 Gbps. For a system with the capacity of 80 Gbps is achieved by wavelength division multiplexing of two 40 Gbps channels and fixed fiber length of 50 km/span. Dispersion is mitigated by fiber Bragg grating (FBG) with post compensation and nonlinear effects are reduced using Dicode. We evaluated the performance of three schemes in terms of bit error rate (BER) and Q factor. Numerical simulation results show that Dicode-NRZ provides better tolerance towards dispersion and nonlinearities compared to others and can transmit signal up to 2000 km.

Author Keywords: Wavelength division multiplexed passive optical network (WDM-PON)

articleTitle: Tunability of resonator based photonic crystal switch by elliptical rods
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this paper, we present a design of a photonic crystal optical switch which is based on an elliptical waveguide resonator to get response at optical wavelength (1.55μm). The objective of this work is to obtain desired operating wavelength by introducing the resonator cavity. The cavity is made up of photonic crystal by imparting two rods of elliptical shape. The radius of major and minor axes and refractive index of elliptical rods can be varied. Modifying the major and minor axes of the elliptical rods in resonator and also by decreasing the refractive index optimum results have been obtained. Finite Difference Time Domain software (OptiFDTD™) is implemented to analyze the characteristics of the switch. We perform switching on and off state by applying low pass filter (LPF) and high pass filter (HPF) respectively. Results show that transmitted power with respect to wavelength has been improved by implementing the proposed structure.

articleTitle: THz guidance through hollow-core plastic photonic bandgap fiber: Sensitivity to structural parameters
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We report a numerically obtained design of a hollow-core plastic microstructured optical fiber (HC-pMOF) for efficient high power terahertz (THz) transmission. The effects of fiber's structural parameters on the propagating THz pulse are carried out in detail. The cross-section of HC-pMOF is composed of hexagonally arranged three periodic cladding rings made of air holes embedded in a uniform Teflon matrix. The THz guidance through the central hollow-core is achieved through photonic band-gap (PBG) effect of the periodic cladding structure. The effects of cladding periodicity as well as core size are investigated for broad-band, low-loss and low-dispersive THz wave transmission and the estimated low-loss (<; 0.5 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>) bandwidth is > 450 GHz. Furthermore, we have investigated the effect of introducing a chirp in the air-hole sizes of the periodic cladding.

articleTitle: Imaging cell division in E-coli using white light diffraction phase microscopy
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Quantitative phase imaging (QPI) techniques is an emerging field aimed at studying weakly scattering and absorbing specimens. QPI techniques provide 3-d images with high contrast, compared to qualitative imaging techniques like bright field imaging, phase contrast imaging, differential interference contrast imaging. White light diffraction phase microscopy (wDPM) is one of the QPI techniques which provide both amplitude and phase images simultaneously with single shot. It also uses common path interferometric geometry which provide better temporal sensitivity compared to other interferometric techniques. Also wDPM uses the white light as the illumination source which makes this imaging technique unique in speckle free imaging. The rate of recording the cellular dynamics is only limited by the camera speed. In this work we developed the wDPM techniques and characterized the system in terms of resolution and sensitivity. We also used the Fast phase reconstruction algorithm to reconstruct the 3d phase form the recorded interference pattern. We recorded the interference pattern of E.coli and reconstructed the 3-d phase images with high sensitivity. We also demonstrated the cell division in E.coli using this technique.

articleTitle: Analysis of spatial modal entanglement using perturbation method technique
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this paper, we analyze the problem of generation of spatial mode entangled photon pairs using the perturbation method in a step index profile channel waveguide. It is shown that by a proper design of the channel waveguide it is possible to generate spatial mode entangled pairs of photons using a single QPM grating.

articleTitle: Determination of optical fiber strain in multi-tube cable by finite element analysis and its experimental validation
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We have determined the fiber strain in the optical fiber cable by using FEA. Proper contacts have been applied for all materials and good match has been obtained between FEA results and experimental results.

articleTitle: Development of an FPGA based photon counting detector for balloon flights
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We intend to develop a compact detector for balloon and space flights using off-the-shelf MCPs, CMOS sensors and optics. The detector should be capable of working in direct frame transfer mode as well as photon counting mode for single photon event detection. The identification and centroiding of each photon event is done using an FPGA(Field programmable Gate Array) based data acquisition and real-time processing system. This guarantees a good deal of flexibility allowing easy testing of different algorithms without modifying the external connections, thus maintaining an unaltered system architecture.

articleTitle: Enhanced bandwidth second harmonic generation in a periodically poled tapered KTP waveguide
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this paper we study second harmonic generation in a tapered channel waveguide and show that using a standard single spatial frequency quasi phase matched grating, it is possible to enhance the bandwidth of the nonlinear process. Numerical results are presented to show pump bandwidth of 10 nm for typical tapered waveguide in KTP. The proposed method could be an interesting alternative to chirped QPM gratings for nonlinear interactions in waveguides.

articleTitle: All spherical optical design of an Ultraviolet Cosmic Imager
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We propose to place a wide-field ultraviolet (UV) imager (Lunar Ultraviolet Cosmic Imager - LUCI) on the Moon to observe in the near-UV wavelength band (200 to 300 nm). LUCI is a Cassegrain telescope with a field of view of half a degree and a total weight of less than two kg. The science goals include observations of variable stars, transients (supernovae, novae, etc.) and possible detection of near-Earth asteroids. LUCI will fly as a payload on the Team INDUS entry to the Google Lunar XPRIZE (GLXP) challenge to launch and land a robotic spacecraft on the Moon. Here we will discuss about the all spherical optical design, in order to realize the proposed UV imager in a very cost effective and easier way.

articleTitle: FITC doped fluorescent silica nanoparticles based optical fiber sensor for copper (II) detection
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We have demonstrated a fast, sensitive fluorescent tapered tip optical fiber (TTOF) sensor to detect copper (Cu (II)) ions. The principle of detection is based on fluorescent quenching of fluorescein isothiocynate (FITC) doped fluorescent silica nanoparticles (FSi) by Cu(II) ions. TTOF was functionalized with FITC doped fluorescent silica nanoparticles (FSi), as transduction element. Amine functionalized FSi nanoparticles are immobilized on aminosilanised tapered tip using glutaraldehyde treatment. Cu (II) ions which form chelation with amines quench the fluorescence (FL) of the FSi nanoparticles. Detection capacity down to 0.25 μM for copper ions has been achieved in this configuration.

articleTitle: Design of octagonal core micro-cladding leakage channel fiber with low bending loss
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We design a large mode area (LMA) micro-cladding leakage channel fiber (LCF) with an octagonal shaped core for 1.064 μm wavelength. Our numerical simulation shows that very low bending loss at small bend radius can be achieved by scaling up the micro-cladding elements of LCF. Further, the proposed fiber exhibits novel properties such as large effective area (1287 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) and very low bending loss of 5.58 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> dB/m for a bending radius of 5 cm. These interesting properties of the proposed LCF pave the way for developing a compact high power fiber laser and amplifier.

articleTitle: Refractive index sensor based on a silica microsphere whispering gallery mode resonator
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We investigated the excitation of whispering gallery modes (WGMs) in a silica microsphere by evanescent field coupling method using a ~2 micrometer diameter fiber taper. Based on this configuration we have developed a sensitive refractometric sensor and observed a red-shift of the WGM resonances with the increase of the surrounding medium refractive index. A sensitivity of ~114 nanometer per RIU has been achieved in the range of refractive indices from 1.3963 to 1.4004.

articleTitle: Few-cycle pulse generation using low confinement loss solid-core photonic quasi-crystal fiber
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We design a solid-core photonic quasi-crystal fiber (SC-PQF) of 6-fold for a wide range of operating wavelengths from 0.3 to 5 μm. Further, we explore the various optical properties, namely, birefringence, group velocity dispersion, confinement loss and nonlinearity for the proposed SC-PQF. We achieve a low dispersion of -13 ps<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/km and a high nonlinearity of 480 W<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> for 0.3 μm wavelength. By exploiting these optical properties, we numerically demonstrate the generation of few-cycle optical pulses of pulse width 4.7 fs from 30 fs input pulse using the higher order soliton pulse compression technique.

articleTitle: Dynamic signal sensing using fiber Bragg grating sensor and interferometric interrogation
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We report our recent experimental studies on phase generated carrier (PGC) based fiber Mach-Zehnder interferometer (F-MZI) interrogation technique for fiber Bragg grating (FBG) sensors. Interferometric techniques such as F-MZI have emerged as most sensitive and accurate technique for demodulation of signal generated by FBGs. F-MZIs are widely used for dynamic strain measurement applications such as vibration analysis, hydrophones, and acoustic emission studies. But, a fiber interferometer is inherently very sensitive to surrounding parameters of temperatures, pressure, and air currents which makes it unsuitable to be used directly as FBG wavelength shift demodulator. So, a PGC is incorporated in MZI to remove these influences. This paper shows the experimental results which supports PGC based demodulation scheme for dynamic signal sensing. FFT based noise elimination technique has also been used here to remove unwanted surrounding and system noises. We have also compared this PGC based F-MZI with CCD spectrometer for demodulation of dynamic signals generated by FBG sensor.

articleTitle: Absolute concentration measurements of bacterial CO2 emission using a 2004 nm vertical cavity surface emitting tunable diode laser
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This paper reports the use of tunable diode laser absorption spectroscopy to make absolute measurement of the concentration of carbon dioxide (CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) emitted by E. coli and lactic acid bacteria (LAB) at different stages of their growth cycle. The emission wavelength of a 2004 nm vertical cavity surface emitting laser diode is scanned across the R16 rotation-vibration line of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> at 2003.5 nm (4991.259 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>) by current tuning. Direct detection is performed to recover the lineshape accurately and the absolute values of the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> concentration are extracted over the growth cycle of the bacteria. The time-varying CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions agree well with theoretical models available in the literature. The calibration-free nature of these measurements is particularly important for such experiments.

articleTitle: Novel spot-size converters for Silicon photonics
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this paper we have proposed a novel spot-size converter without using a reverse taper. The converter is realized by using a phase matched multilayer array with the Silicon nanowire. Finite Element method and Least Squares Boundary Residual method have been used for the analysis. Results show significant improved coupling which increases from 1% in case of direct nanowire coupling to 53% when the array is butt coupled to a fiber.

articleTitle: Effects of different structures of photonic crystals on optical sensor designing applications
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In Photonics, light with varying optical properties and characteristics can be made useful for applications involving optical sensor designing by changing its flow through different media with differing Refractive Indices. What seems to be a neglecting factor is that of choosing optimum structure for these optical sensor designing applications. This paper aims at addressing this issue of using non optimum structures for various optical sensor designing applications. Effects of these structures are studied and structures with good sensitivity and Q-factor are considered. Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) is used for mathematical modeling of the structures and MEEP is used to create and simulate the structure taking common platforms to analyze Transmission Spectrum. Results show some structures are better than those which are being used now in various optical sensor designs.

articleTitle: U-bent fiberoptic evanescent wave absorbance plasmonic sandwich biosensor: Silver based signal enhancement
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this study, silver enhanced labelling method was employed in evanescent wave absorbance based fiber optic immunosensor for improving the sensitivity of biomolecular detection. A multi-dimensional sensitive and specific detection of Human Immunoglobulin G (HIgG) is illustrated by exploiting: (i) U-bent optical probe with enhanced evanescent absorbance sensitivity, (ii) Highly specific sandwich immunoassay format, (iii) Plasmonic particles (AuNP) having high extinction properties as labels and (iv) Enhanced extinction due to silver deposition on catalytic labels. A detection sensitivity of 0.02 A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>3<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0nm</inf> / log (ng/ml) was obtained using sandwich assay for HIgG detection. A 25-fold improvement in sensitivity was achieved using silver enhancement technique.

articleTitle: Investigation of optimum fiber types for high speed RZ-DQPSK transmission systems
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This paper presents a simulative analysis of 40Gb/s Return-to-Zero Differential Quadrature Phase Shift Keying (RZ-DQPSK) scheme under Self Phase Modulation (SPM) and Amplified Spontaneous Emission (ASE) over three commonly utilized fiber types like Standard Single Mode Fiber (SMF), True-Wave Reduced Slope (TW-RS) and Large Effective Area Fibers (LEAF). The RZ-DQPSK is tested with 33% and 67% duty cycles. This analysis helps in selecting the best type of fiber for long-haul communication.

articleTitle: Investigation of hybrid planar plasmonic waveguide
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Performance of planar hybrid plasmonic waveguide has been investigated in detail considering its structural and material aspects. Mode properties of hybrid metal insulator (HMI) waveguide has been studied at 1550 nm wavelength using frequency domain electromagnetic solver of CST microwave studio. Investigation reveals that this waveguide provides large propagation length and deep sub wavelength confinement in low dielectric layers. This kind of waveguide overcomes the limitations of conventional plasmonic waveguides and instigates many applications such as nano lasers, couplers, dividers, optical interconnects, bio sensors and optical trapping etc.

articleTitle: Improved design and analysis of 2D hexagonal photonic crystal structure based channel drop filter for optical communication system
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A improved design of channel drop filter is proposed based on two-dimensional (2D) hexagonal photonic crystal ring resonators. The transmission spectra of PCRR configuration has been investigated by using the Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method in a Hexagonal lattice GaAs rods photonic crystal structure. The Photonic Bandgap (PBG) of the designed structure is calculated by Plane Wave Expansion (PWE) method. In this paper PhC design has been optimized for telecommunication wavelength 1511 nm. The number of rods in X and Z directions are 19 and 23, with lattice constant 0.540 nm and 0.1 μm rod radius. The designed structure is useful for CWDM optical communication systems and may serve as a key component in photonic integrated circuits. Scatterer rod radius analysis is also done in this paper to improve the dropping efficiency around 99%. The device is ultra compact with the overall size around 127 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Characteristics of square-lattice microstructured optical fibers: An analytical field approach
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Using our earlier developed analytical field model we have studied the modal properties of index-guiding or solid-core microstructured optical fibers with square-lattice of circular voids or air-holes in the photonic crystal cladding made with high nonlinearity non-silica glass composition material as well as fused silica glass. For comparison the numerical simulation results have been included.

articleTitle: Optimizing focused pump beam characteristics for maximum correlated photon pairs in non-collinear degenerate parametric down conversion
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We investigate the methods to obtain maximum correlated photon pairs generated in Type I spontaneous parametric down conversion (SPDC) with focused pump beam. We study the effect of pump focusing on the photon collection efficiency of signal and idler modes. The correlated photon pair collection efficiency decreases asymptotically with input pump beam focusing parameter [1]. The results obtained here are expected to be useful in designing appropriate optical fibers for generating efficient entangled photon sources for quantum information applications.

articleTitle: A novel frequency detector for DP-QPSK receivers using sine-cosine sampling method
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: To cater to the demand for ever increasing Internet traffic, on-off keying over multi-mode fiber is expected to be replaced with coherent signaling over single mode fiber in short-reach optical interconnects. One of the key challenges faced at the receiver-end is the recovery of the frequency and phase of the transmitter laser. We propose a novel frequency detector that uses sine-cosine sampling method which can be used in a carrier phase recovery and compensation loop. System level simulations of the proposed detector show promising results.

articleTitle: Residual phase gradients in optical null interference sensing rotating optical field in a nulling Sagnac interferometer
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A scheme to sense the residual phase gradients in an optical interference of two out-of-phase Gaussian beams is proposed. Its implementation by detecting the residual phase gradient as an optical field rotation in a Sagnac interferometer, configured to provide a null output is presented.

articleTitle: Sensitivity analysis for photonic crystal waveguide based refractive index sensing using plane wave expansion simulations
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Photonic crystal waveguide for refractive index sensing is investigated. Plane wave expansion method, which is fast and suitable for analyzing periodic structures, is used to estimate the functionality for refractive index sensing. Dispersion diagram is obtained to quantify transmittance and to determine the cut-off wavelength, which shifts for a small change in refractive index in the voids. It has been proposed that ring-type line defect photonic crystal waveguide has relatively better sensitivity for sensing applications as compared to the conventional line defect waveguide.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of optical QAM scheme using an electro-optic microring resonator
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We propose an optical 16-QAM generation scheme based on pockel effect induced in a single electro-optic microring resonator by the incoming 4 bit binary data. The design of the resonator for achieving this and the 16-QAM constellation that can be realized is presented. This scheme can provide small footprint and low power consumption with a potential for realizing green elastic optical communication.

articleTitle: Silicon photonic integrated circuit for multi-mode fiber link
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We design and simulate a novel Silicon Photonic Integrated Transceiver circuit for data transmission by multiplexing of random spatial modes in a multi-mode fiber (MMF) and data recovery using adaptive signal processing at the receiver.

articleTitle: Design of a Si-EO polymer hybrid WH/TS encoder with transformation optics based waveguide coupler
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Design of a dynamic WH/TS optical encoder along with a coupler for fiber to chip mode conversion is presented. The encoding device utilizes fast EO tuning of defect mode of an EO polymer infiltrated 1D Si photonic crystal resonator. The TM waveguide coupler providing mode size matching from 9μm to 240nm is designed using transformational optics with additional Si-air layers for antireflection. In this encoder, chip duration, wavelength selection and time gating functions can be programmed to provide adaptive 2D OCDMA encoding that ensures low power, low cost upgrade in capacity of standard 10Gbps systems in access networks to a minimum of 100Gbps.

articleTitle: FCA based two photon absorption and simulation of Si waveguide to device optical logic gates
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In the presented work, the concept of two photon absorption has been realised, through the solution of TPA equation. Considering realistic assumption, the free carrier absorption effect has also been included in the study. For comparative analysis, different silicon rib waveguide structures have been considered. The mode profile corresponding to each structure has been simulated using the Lumerical software tool. The power transfer characteristics for different waveguides have been plotted, which imparts knowledge on the effect of varying effect area of the waveguides and the FCA effect on the power curve. Finally the paper describes the design of optical logic gates, through the application of TPA. Optical logic gates are required to perform high speed optical signal processing, digitally. It forms a major area of research at present.

articleTitle: Sensing near the liquid:liquid interface remotely via ultrafast pump probe study
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Ultrafast pump-probe technique has been invoked to understand the liquid:liquid interface by using a cyanine dye dissolved in dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), interfaced with neat diethyl-ether (Et2O). We show that the dynamics of the dye gets slow down on moving from the bulk dye solution in DMSO towards the interface with neat-diethyl ether. Hence we get an alternate picture of interface by looking at the time constants. Four time constants were used for fitting the experimental data which are assigned to be coherent artifact, vibrational cooling, intermediate state time and finally ground state recovery time. The drastic change in signal was observed at a distance of 0.1 mm from the interface. The decreasing time constants from bulk to near interfaced solution strongly suggests involvement of heterogeneity in the system because of the penetration of diethyl ether through the interface into the DMSO layer where the dye is dissolved, which strongly affects the dynamics at near the interface of the DMSO with neat-diethyl ether layer (at 0.1 mm distance from the interface).

articleTitle: Development of a 535 nm frequency doubled fiber laser with enhanced spatial coherence for diabetic retinopathy
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We demonstrate a continuous wave (CW) fiber laser with 2W output power at 1070 nm with 58 % slope efficiency, and have used the same to generate 535 nm radiation suitable for retinal photocoagulation.

articleTitle: Dissipative soliton mediated dispersive wave in silicon-based waveguides
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We numerically demonstrate that, under the perturbation of third order dispersion, dissipative solution in active medium can generate strong dispersive waves in the form of radiation. We propose a realistic Si-based waveguide which can excite such dissipative soliton mediated energy radiation. The phase matching condition is studied to explore the underlying physics of this phenomenon.

articleTitle: Entanglement and its role on the capacity of noisy two-Pauli channels
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The discovery of super dense coding paved the way for future quantum communications that exploit the power of entanglement. The protocol lets users communicate two classical bits using a pre-shared entangled pair of qubits called a Bell pair. However, the protocol assumes that a noiseless channel exists between end users. Moreover, perfect Bell pairs may not always be created in any experimental set up. We study the single shot communication properties of partially entangled Werner state and partially entangled pure bipartite states by considering the two-Pauli channel. The two-Pauli channel accommodates for both bit flips and phase flips that qubits may suffer during transmission. Quantification of entanglement is done via entanglement of formation and its dependence on capacity is analyzed.

articleTitle: Supercontinuum generation in silver doped photonic crystal fiber
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Silver doped photonic crystal fibers offer an additional control over the Kerr nonlinearity of core glass. We investigated numerically the optical properties and found an octave-spanning super continum where the visible region is dominated by Raman induced blue shifting and longer wavelength edge by dispersive wave generation.

articleTitle: Determination of transformer oil age using long period grating
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This paper presents about the determination of age of transformer oil using long period grating. The aging of the oil leads to change in refractive index of cladding, which shifts the Bragg wavelength of the long period gratings. The sensitivity is higher with the long period grating in comparison to the others.

articleTitle: Exploring the critical role of detection aperture in thermal lens measurements
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The critical role of the detection aperture size on the measurement of thermal lens signals has been explored by using mode-mismatched pump-probe thermal lens spectroscopy in pure methanol. Femtosecond laser pulses at 1560 nm are used to create thermal lens signal, which is simultaneously probed by a collinear 780 nm pulse train through a partially open aperture of different sizes placed after the sample. The trend in the time resolved thermal lens signals reveals that aperture size allowing less than half of the incident probe light is critical in providing accuracy of the thermal lens spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Self amplification of super-critical angle fluorescence using laser dye, in presence and absence of nano-scatterers
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We report on self-amplification of super-critical angle fluorescence (SAF) and its anomalous behavior in presence of scatterers in comparison to conventional random lasers. We propose a mechanism of self-amplification which explains this anomalous behavior.

articleTitle: Generation of stable cavity soliton in vertical cavity surface emitting laser: A variational approach
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The existence and stability of multi-dimensional spatially dissipative solitons, commonly known as cavity solitons, is studied. Variational method is applied to obtain the evolution dynamics of (D+1)-dimensional system of cubic-quintic complex Ginzburg-Landau equation. The stability criteria is established using the Lyapunov and Hurwitz conditions. Split step Fourier method is applied to validate the results of analytical study.

articleTitle: Propagation of a periodic sequence of Gaussian pulses through coaxial fiber for pulse repetition rate multiplication
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: When a series of pulses pass through a first order linear dispersive media, the spectral components of pulse train acquire phase delays which cause repetition of input pulse at certain distances. This effect, referred to as ‘Talbot effect’ can be used to achieve pulse repetition rate multiplication for use in high bit-rate optical fibers for high speed data transfer. In this paper we present coaxial fiber as first order linear dispersive media for achieving pulse repetition rate multiplication. Its dispersion characteristics and its response to a series of Gaussian pulses have been studied in detail.

articleTitle: Quantitative imaging of yeast cells using transport of intensity equation
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In biology most microscopy specimens, in particular living cells are transparent. In cell imaging, it is hard to create an image of a cell which is transparent with a very small refractive index change with respect to the surrounding media. Various techniques like addition of staining and contrast agents, markers have been applied in the past for creating contrast. Many of the staining agents or markers are not applicable to live cell imaging as they are toxic. In this paper, we report theoretical and experimental results from quantitative phase imaging of yeast cells with a commercial bright field microscope. We reconstruct the phase of cells non-interferometrically based on the transport of intensity equations (TIE). This technique estimates the axial derivative from positive through-focus intensity measurements. This technique allows phase imaging using a regular microscope with white light illumination. We demonstrate nano-metric depth sensitivity in imaging live yeast cells using this technique. Experimental results will be shown in the paper demonstrating the capability of the technique in 3-D volume estimation of living cells. This real-time imaging technique would be highly promising in real-time digital pathology applications, screening of pathogens and staging of diseases like malaria as it does not need any preprocessing of samples.

articleTitle: Low loss mode multiplexer de-multiplexer for mode division multiplexing over two mode fiber
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Mode Division Multiplexing (MDM) over Few Mode Fiber (FMF) enhances the capacity of an optical fiber system by providing additional degrees of freedom in the form of modes which are selectively excited at the transmitter and selectively detected at the receiver. The key to capitalize on such a system is implementation of low loss mode multiplexer (mux) and de-multiplexer (de-mux) with low modal crosstalk. In this paper we dwell upon design and software implementation of such a low loss mode mux and de-mux for Two Mode Fiber (TMF).

articleTitle: Dissipative soliton in optical fiber with multiphoton absorption and random dispersion
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The effect of random dispersion, multiphoton absorption on the pulse propagating through a fiber having cubic-quintic nonlinearity has been studied. The detrimental effects of two photon absorption and three photon absorption on the pulse have been discussed. The presence of quintic nonlinearity causes the pulse to oscillate. The random dispersion in the system contributes to the random oscillations in the pulse parameters. Inspite of the dissipative nature of the system due to multi photon absorption and random dispersion, solitons can still be generated by the injection of proper gain.

articleTitle: Design of Hybrid (Refractive-Diffractive) Petzval projection lens system
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this framework, the Refractive elements and the Diffractive element has been combined to explore the uniqueness of two domains into one Hybrid system. It was thus targeted to achromatize the optical system and to reduce the overall weight of the system, by incorporating lesser number of optical components to provide similar system performance using Hybrid optical design method. A 60 mm, f/2 Hybrid Petzval projection system with four components covering a 15° field of view has been presented here. The diffractive surface is introduced on the rear surface of the 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> lens having 71 zones. The minimum zone size is approximately 2.42274 μm and the total chromatic focal shift is limited to 46.12 μm. Optimization and analysis has been performed on Zemax® and the corresponding results are shown.

articleTitle: One step 3D hologram master origination for security applications
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Optical security is a promising technology and widely used due to their parallel and high speed processing capabilities. Holograms are widely used as one of the most trusted tools for product authentication and security. Now the demand for hologram as a security authentication tool is increasing due to its higher data density, visual appeal and cheap at the mass production. It is commonly believed that holograms cannot be counterfeited. Though, due to the revolutionary development in digital image processing technologies, it is rather easy to counterfeit the holograms that are commonly used today in security applications. But the conventional recorded 3D holograms are still are very complicated to counterfeit as it requires a certain level of expertise and non availability of digital tools. This paper describes a one step 3D hologram master origination process and its analysis.

articleTitle: Highly sensitive refractive index sensor based on Bragg grating in metallic-hole microstructured optical fiber
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We present a theoretical comparative study of a highly sensitive Bragg grating sensor written in a microstructured optical fiber with bare and metallic voids or holes. Based on the full vector effective index method and the coupled mode theory our simulations show that the device is maximum sensitive for small metal thickness showing nearly double sensitive at 10 nm metal thickness as compared to that for the bare hole. This highest sensitivity is comparable to the maximum sensitivity reported for the pure surface plasmon polariton based Bragg gratin sensors and, unlike the later, the modes are easy to excite for the present sensor. Owing to the reflective mode operation the device is ideally suited for highly sensitive, remote deep sea and oil well sensing applications.

articleTitle: A novel method of rotation sensing by semiconductor ring laser gyroscope
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We propose an alternate method to sense inertial rotation using semiconductor ring laser gyroscope (SRLG). We show that inertial rotation causes change in the magnitude of voltage across the terminals of semiconductor gain medium which can be measured externally to determine angular rotation velocity. The resonant oscillating frequency of the counter-traveling waves are not involved in the measurement which leads to elimination of lock-in in the gyro. The mathematical analysis and simulation results of the proposed method are also shown.

articleTitle: An all-optical NOT logic operation based on a chloroform filled geometrically asymmetric triangular triple-core PCF
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We present an all optical NOT logic operation based on a geometrically asymmetric triangular triple core photonic crystal fiber (ATPCF), where the guiding cores are filled with highly nonlinear liquid chloroform. By employing the finite element method, necessary optical parameters of the proposed geometry are determined. The steering characteristics which attributes the critical power necessary for the control signal is obtained numerically via coupled nonlinear Schrodinger equations. Through extinction ratio calculations, the Boolean operation of NOT logic gate is illustrated with an appropriate control signal. This study accomplish the idea of an efficient NOT logic operation based on ATPCF geometry. As well as provides the sensitive dependence of geometrical asymmetry on input conditions for performing logic operations.

Author Keywords: logic gates and split step Fourier method

articleTitle: Fiber optic evanescent wave sensor for the measurement of curcumin
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A fiber optic technique for the measurement of very low concentrations of curcumin is presented. The fiber optic sensor outlined here is based on evanescent field absorption. A short uncladded portion of a plastic cladded silica fiber acts as the sensing region. In order to enhance the performance of the sensor, neera was used as an additional reagent for the measurement of curcumin. The experimental results clearly establish the usefulness of the present technique for the measurement of very low concentrations of curcumin.

articleTitle: Development of a flyash concentration measurement method based on light scattering techniques
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Flyash free fuel-gas produced by burning coal in a pressurized fluidized bed gasifier is essential for a proper functioning of a power-plant gas turbine. A reliable measurement technique/instrument is required for estimating the particle concentration at locations, such as at the entry and exit of the filter system. Feasibility of optical techniques based on Mie scattering and extinction in order to determine flyash concentration in an exhaust at different flow rates is studied using the experimental setup developed in-house. These optical properties are measured for flyash particles with diameter ranging from 20 to 200 μm along with air flow using a continuous-wave green laser (wavelength around 530 nm). Prototype instrument is designed and a uniform feed rate ranges from 2 to 18 g/min is achieved. Scattered signals at different angles are presented as a function of varying feed rates of flyash particles. Extinction signal as a function of time for different feed rate is also presented. Time-averaged, extinction signal based measurements were also in qualitative agreement with light scattering based measurements. It is also possible to measure extinction signal with different particle sizes and feed-rates, representing variation in flyash concentration.

articleTitle: Study of hole taper and HAZ width in laser drilling of black acrylic
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The present work is on the spot drilling of black acrylic (PMMA) using a Diode laser of wavelength 809.40 nm. The design of experimental layouts for drilling has been done using the Taguchi's method. After drilling, the hole taper and the heat-affected-zone (HAZ) of the drilled holes have been measured. The influence of the experimentally controllable parameters on the measured outputs have been analyzed and discussed.

articleTitle: Effect of dielectric nanoparticles on light extraction efficiency of OLED
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We report enhancement in light extraction efficiency of organic light emitting diode (OLED) using dielectric nano-particles between glass substrate and anode. The nano-particles acted as a scattering medium for the light trapped in waveguiding modes of the device. The simulation and analysis of design has been carried out by finite difference time domain (FDTD) method. Effects of various parameters like diameter, interparticle separation and refractive index of nanoparticles were studied. The maximum enhancement in light extraction efficiency of 1.7 times has been achieved.

articleTitle: Modified electric arc discharge technique for fabrication of long period gratings in air-core fibers: Effect of air pressure inside fiber holes
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this paper we present the modified Electric Arc Discharge useful to the fabrication of Long period gratings in hollow core fibers. The proposed approach consists in electric Arc Discharge assisted by air pressure inside core and cladding holes of the fiber lattice structure. Here, the vital role of air pressure in the holes of the fibers is experimentally investigated. Our results show that the proposed approach successfully permit the production of Long Period Grating (LPG) in the hollow core air silica photonic bandgap fiber.

articleTitle: Studies on the propagation of orbital angular momentum beams through optical fibers with different index profiles
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We report our studies on the propagation of light beams possessing orbital angular momentum (OAM) through optical fibers having different index profiles with the emphasis on stable propagation. Simulation results on propagation characteristics of OAM beam in different index fibers are presented. We also present preliminary experimental results validating the same. Presented study is expected to be useful in configuring an all-fiber cavity for a fiber laser with OAM beam output that is desired for communication and high power fiber laser applications.

articleTitle: Random and perturbed band-edge lasing in an amplifying quasi-periodic microdroplet array
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We demonstrate the experimental implementation and theoretical analysis of random lasing and perturbed band-edge lasing in a linear array of monodisperse amplifying micro-resonators. Transfer matrix calculations with gain conclude that a higher threshold is required for triggering perturbed band edge lasing compared to random lasing in a quasi-periodic system. Statistical analyses of lasing spectra and the intensity differences of lasing peaks of perturbed band edge and random lasing modes conclusively indicate the experimental realization of a quasi-periodic system.

articleTitle: Curcumin doped silica xerogel for sensing applications
publicationTitle: 2015 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Present work reports the preparation of natural dye Curcumin doped silica xerogel and its application towards fluoride ion sensing in aqueous media. Curcumin doped silica xerogel film was observed to possess a clear absorbance peak of 441 nm. The sensitive response of the xerogel film immobilized on a microscopic slide was registered by changes in the absorbance values with respect to change in fluoride concentration.
